files.Title: ReactorSockets.CloseReason
files.Summary: Why a Link closed, defined and kept stable by this library rather than borrowed from a platform enumeration (ADR 0008): a consumer's permanent logic switches on this instead of a that differs between Windows and Unix. The exact travels in the emitted at the same moment, linked to this only by the Link and the Pump it happened in.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DatagramSessionOptions
files.Summary: The construction surface of a (ADR 0012): the shared L0 budget composed in as , plus the knobs this profile alone has. Composed rather than inherited, so that nothing protocol-specific here can ever leak into and turn it into the base class ADR 0011 refused.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DatagramSessionReactor
files.Summary: The datagram Session profile (ADR 0009): Sessions established over UDP, addressed as Peers, driven by a single synchronous from the consumer's own loop. It carries the handshake and everything that guards it — the stateless cookie, the amplification bound, version and capacity refusals, session identity and demultiplexing — and the data plane behind it: packet records in four sequence Spaces, one per , fragmentation of reliable Messages, acknowledgement and retransmission, heartbeats, Goodbye, interruption and Resume.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DeliveryMode
files.Summary: Which of a datagram Session's four delivery modes carries a Message sent through (ADR 0009). See docs/delivery-modes.md for the consumer-facing guide to choosing one and the full guarantees each mode makes: ordering, duplicate suppression, and what a late arrival does. Each mode is carried in its own Space.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DiagnosticFormatter
files.Summary: The one authoritative rendering of a to text (ADR 0005, ADR 0013), so a structured Sink consumes the typed fields and never formats, and a text Sink gets this library's wording rather than inventing its own. Holds no state: nothing is allocated until is called, and a consumer who never formats pays nothing.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DiagnosticId
files.Summary: A closed, permanent enumeration of diagnostic causes with explicit values in reserved blocks — common 1-99, Raw 100-199, datagram session 200-299, stream session 300-399 (ADR 0013) — so a future insertion cannot silently renumber an id a consumer has persisted. There is no None or Unknown member and zero is never used: every has a cause by construction.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DiagnosticLevel
files.Summary: The minimum severity a Sink was installed to receive. Ordered by ascending severity so that a level is enabled when it is at least as severe as the installed MinimumLevel.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DiagnosticRecord
files.Summary: A single diagnostic emitted to an Sink: a closed , its fixed , a tagged subject — none, Link, Source or Peer (ADR 0013) — and two numeric slots whose meaning is documented per member. No strings, no object[], no closures — everything here lives on the stack and is built only after passes.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DiagnosticSubjectKind
files.Summary: Which field of a 's tagged subject is populated (ADR 0013). A record has exactly one subject, so a Sink or formatter switches on this rather than checking several optional fields for which one is set.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.DisconnectReason
files.Summary: Why a Peer's Session ended, defined and kept stable by this library rather than borrowed from a platform enumeration. Deliberately not shared with the Raw profile's (ADR 0008): most of the members a Session needs are protocol vocabulary Raw can never produce, and a single shared enumeration would leave one profile documenting members it cannot emit.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.IReactorDiagnostics
files.Summary: The Diagnostic Sink contract. Implementations are called synchronously, on the consumer's thread, inside Pump — a Sink that stalls stalls the Frame, and a Sink that throws is caught, counted as SinkFaulted, and disabled for the life of the Reactor (ADR 0005). Calling back into the Reactor from a Sink is a programmer error and throws.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.LinkCounters
files.Summary: A point-in-time snapshot of one Link's counters (ADR 0013): monotonic figures running from that Link's registration, with no reset, fetched by value and keyed by — there is no accessor that enumerates every Link's counters in one call.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.LinkId
files.Summary: A Link's identity: the Reactor that issued it, a zero-based slot index, and a generation counter that increments when the slot is reused, so a stale held past a Link's close compares unequal to whatever now occupies that slot (ADR 0014) rather than aliasing it.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.Logging.LoggerSink
files.Summary: An Sink that writes each record to an . The message is 's text, never wording of this package's own, and the state carries the record's typed fields for a structured provider. One type serves every profile: install one per Reactor, each over a logger with its own category from one , and every Reactor writes one stream with each record attributed by category.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.PeerCounters
files.Summary: A point-in-time snapshot of one Peer's counters (ADR 0013): monotonic figures running from that Peer's establishment, with no reset, fetched by value and keyed by — mirrors 's Raw-profile shape and the same "no accessor enumerates every Peer's counters in one call" rule.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.PeerId
files.Summary: A Peer's identity inside this process: the Reactor that issued it, a zero-based Slot index, and a generation counter that increments when the Slot is reused, so a stale held past a Peer's close compares unequal to whatever now occupies that Slot (ADR 0007) rather than aliasing it. Shared by both Session profiles (ADR 0010), exactly as is the Raw profile's.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.RawEvent
files.Summary: One event drained from a . A ref struct because aliases the frame arena directly and must never outlive the Frame it was drained in (ADR 0008). determines exactly which other fields are populated — the kinds are , , , , , and — the complete Raw profile roster.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.RawEventEnumerator
files.Summary: The zero-allocation enumerator returns. A ref struct so that a foreach over it can yield — itself a ref struct — without a heap-allocated IEnumerator<T>, following the same pattern as 's own enumerator.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.RawEventKind
files.Summary: Which kind of a drained event is (ADR 0008). comes from a listening Link, from dialling, and from stream reads, and from partial sends.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.RawReactor.MaxUdpDatagramSize
files.Summary: The largest payload a UDP datagram can carry over IPv4, and this Reactor's default scratch buffer size and arena floor: a Segment is as large as one read, so the arena must hold at least one (ADR 0012). An IPv6 datagram can carry up to 65 527 bytes, more than this bound.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.RawReactor
files.Summary: The escape hatch (ADR 0007): a consumer registers UDP sockets at runtime, gets a back for each, and advances everything with a single synchronous call from their own loop. Nothing is delivered except in response to a call the consumer made, on the thread that constructed this Reactor. TCP joins the datagram surface here: a listening Link and the connections it accepts are registered and admitted the same way, and a stream Link's reads drain as and exactly like a datagram Link's. A stream Link's takes what the socket will take and reports the count, arming exactly one when it took fewer bytes than offered; sends this Link's own FIN while it stays open for reading.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.ReactorCounters
files.Summary: A point-in-time snapshot of the Reactor-scope counters (ADR 0013): monotonic figures running from construction, with no reset. Fetched by value so nothing lets a consumer hold a pointer into live state across a Pump; diffing two snapshots gives everything a reset would, from state the consumer already owns.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.ReactorOptions
files.Summary: The budget L0 spends inside a Pump, shared by every profile. Composed as a member into each profile's options type rather than inherited from a base (ADR 0012) — nothing protocol-specific may ever enter this type, since a knob two of three profiles need is exactly what would turn it into the base class ADR 0011 refused.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.Result
files.Summary: The outcome of an operation whose failures are the caller's to check rather than the runtime's to throw — a wrong-kind call on a Link (Send on a datagram Link) or a send the remote end or the network refused. names the illegality or the platform failure in prose; there is no error code enumeration here because, unlike , nothing about this failure needs to survive as permanent public API — a consumer branches on and logs or surfaces as-is.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.SendOutcome
files.Summary: The outcome of one call. A bare enum rather than a result struct (unlike ): a Session-level send has no partial-completion quantity worth reporting back — the framed Message either fit in the Peer's retention region whole, or it did not, so the outcome is the whole story.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.SendResult
files.Summary: The outcome of one call. Unlike , a stream send has a quantity worth reporting even on success: the Reactor holds no outbound bytes (ADR 0008), so Send takes what the socket will take right now and hands back the count — the caller keeps whatever was not taken, and is how it learns how much that is.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.SessionEvent
files.Summary: One event drained from a Session Reactor. A ref struct because aliases the frame arena directly, and must never outlive the Frame it was drained in (ADR 0008). determines exactly which other fields are populated.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.SessionEventEnumerator
files.Summary: The zero-allocation enumerator every Session Reactor's Drain returns (ADR 0010), shared by both profiles via rather than duplicated per profile. A ref struct so that a foreach over it can yield — itself a ref struct — without a heap-allocated IEnumerator<T>, following the same pattern as 's own enumerator.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.SessionEventKind
files.Summary: Which kind of was drained, and therefore which of its fields carry meaning. Shared by both Session profiles (ADR 0010).

files.Title: ReactorSockets.Source
files.Summary: Who a datagram claims to be from — an unauthenticated hint about origin, never an identity (ADR 0014). Carried on the record path as a value type: { family, 16 address bytes, scope id, port }, roughly 56 bytes, so a Diagnostic or an Event never allocates to name a Source.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.SourceFamily
files.Summary: The address family of a , carried as an explicit tag rather than inferred from the address bytes (ADR 0014). With DualMode never set, nothing in a 16-byte field distinguishes a zero-padded IPv4 address from an IPv6 one.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.StreamSessionOptions
files.Summary: The construction surface of a (ADR 0011): the shared L0 budget composed in as , plus the knobs this profile alone has. Composed rather than inherited, so that nothing protocol-specific here can ever leak into and turn it into the base class ADR 0011 refused.

files.Title: ReactorSockets.StreamSessionReactor
files.Summary: The stream Session profile (ADR 0010): Sessions established over TCP, addressed as Peers, delivering u32 length-prefixed Messages rather than the byte runs the transport gives. Construction validates and its allocation bill and binds the declared endpoint set; each Peer is carried through the handshake to an established Session. Each established Peer reassembles Messages in its own persistent receive buffer and delivers each whole one as a event copied into the shared frame arena.
